12. As against the aforesaid submissions of the learned Counsels for the defence, Mr Bashir Ahmed, the learned Deputy Attorney-General (hereinafter DAG) controverting the argument advanced from the side of the defence submits that in the instant case there is no subsequent embellishment or doubt in believing the prosecution case inasmuch as the informant of this case Md Harun-or-Rashid during his ejahar tried to state the names of the accused persons and identification of the accused at the time of occurrence by the inmates of the house, but due to threatening and undue influence of the Officer-in-charge of Kotwali Police Station, Cumilla, in the F.I.R. there is no mention of the name of accused and recognition of the accused persons by the inmates of the place of occurrence house at the time of occurrence. The learned Deputy Attorney-General in his submission specifically submits that the police from the very beginning of this case has played a foul play in this case in favour of the accused persons, being biased and influenced by them and for the said reason without proper investigation of this case they submitted a final report under section 173 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. In this connection, the learned DAG has pointed out the sketch-map and index of the place of occurrence which were prepared by the police officer who initially investigated the case. In fact, for the place of occurrence house, no sketch-map or index has been prepared, which is admittedly the residence of the deceased Tofazzal Hossain. The learned DAG further submits that, non examination of the deceased's wife namely Shahida Begum also does not bring any presumption in favour of the defence that the wife of the deceased, was intentionally withheld from examination as prosecution witness and there can be no such adverse presumption under section 114(g) of the Evidence Act, 1872 that had she been examined she would not have supported the prosecution case, inasmuch as; Shahida Begum's present husband, to whom she had been married subsequent to the death of Tofazzal Hossain, has forbidden her (Shahida) to depose before the court with regard to the occurrence of this case and to substantiate the. actual facts on behalf of the prosecution during trial, and in support of this, in the original case an application to that effect was filed on 23-11-2006 and that application was perused by the learned trial judge, who has kept it in the record. Therefore, obviously a reasonable cause has been cited from the side of the prosecution as to why Shahida did not depose before the court to corroborate the case of the prosecution. Only because of the fear of social stigma the wife of the deceased Tofazzal is not coming to corroborate the prosecution case. The learned DAG referring two decisions reported in 29 DLR (SC) 256 (para 11) and 7 SCC 295 (para 38) submits that the learned Magistrate after acceptance of the naraji petition rightly has treated the same as complaint petition and thereafter passed an order in respect of sending the case for further investigation under section 190 of the Code of Criminal Procedure to the Criminal Investigation Department (CID), Bangladesh and as because admittedly all the accused persons are previously known to the witnesses, there was no necessity of TIP. It appears from the case records that the condemned-prisoner Md Abu Taher @ Choru Miah, Md A Salam @ Liton, Zahirul Islam @ Zahir and Md Bahar @ Rosen are the co-villagers to the informant as well as the deceased of this case. Not only this, the accused persons are neighbours to the witnesses despite 04 accused persons hails from village Vatpara and Simpur, which are adjacent villages of Joshpur and it is not the case of defence rather they have admitted that the accused of this case are close neighbours of the deceased who are previously known to the inmates of the place of occurrence house. The learned DAG referring a decision of our Apex court reported in 53 DLR AD 1 (para 16) submits that from the testimony of the informant there is a satisfactory explanation from the side of the prosecution as to why in the ejahar there is no mention about identification and names of the assailants who committed the occurrence. 

 46. In respect of another argument of the defence, on non examination of Shahida, wife of Tofazzal, the explanation which is coming from the side of the prosecution is very much acceptable. We have nothing to disagree with the learned DAG as to the non examination of the wife of deceased during trial. Therefore there cannot be any presumption under section 114(g) of the Evidence Act, 1872 that had she been examined she would not have supported the prosecution case.
